subject: English

option_a: Hakim prepares his schoolbag for school.

explanation: All the details show Hakim getting his schoolbag ready. So the main idea is that he prepares for school.

subject: English
question_text: At the pasar malam, Mei Ling bought satay, fruit, and a drink. She enjoyed walking past the busy stalls. What is the main idea?
option_a: Mei Ling visited a pasar malam.

subject: English

option_a: Ravi practises badminton regularly.

subject: English

explanation: The sentence lists different resources available in the library. These details support the main idea that the library offers many learning resources.

subject: English

option_a: Siti cares for her cat.
option_d: Siti forgot to feed the cat.

option_a: People protected themselves from heavy rain.
explanation: The passage explains what people did because of the heavy rain. Those actions support the main idea that they protected themselves from it.

subject: English
question_text: Farid saved RM2 every school day. He wanted to buy a new storybook at the end of the month. What is the main idea?
option_a: Farid is saving money for a storybook.
explanation: The details tell us how much Farid saves and why. The main idea is that he is saving money to buy a storybook.

subject: English
question_text: Nurin and her brother collected plastic bottles at the park. They placed them in a recycling bin. What is the main idea?
option_a: Nurin and her brother helped keep the park clean.
option_b: They threw rubbish on the ground.
option_c: They went to the park to play football.
option_d: They collected leaves for a project.

subject: English
question_text: The canteen serves nasi lemak, noodles, fruit, and sandwiches. Pupils can choose different meals each day. What is the main idea?
option_a: The canteen offers different food choices.
option_c: Pupils must bring food from home.
explanation: The list of meals shows that pupils have several choices. So the main idea is that the canteen offers different kinds of food.

subject: English
question_text: Amir wears a helmet when riding his bicycle. He also checks the brakes before leaving. What is the main idea?
option_a: Amir follows bicycle safety steps.
explanation: Wearing a helmet and checking the brakes are safety actions. They support the main idea that Amir follows bicycle safety steps.

subject: English
question_text: The class planted flowers beside the school hall. They watered them and added compost to the soil. What is the main idea?
option_a: The class is caring for a flower garden.
option_b: The class is painting the school hall.
option_c: The class is cutting down trees.
option_d: The class is buying flowers from a shop.
explanation: Planting, watering, and adding compost are all parts of caring for a garden. That is the main idea of the passage.

subject: English
question_text: During recess, Adam noticed a younger pupil drop his lunch box. Adam picked it up, returned it, and helped gather the food containers. Which sentence best states the main idea?
option_a: Adam was helpful to a younger pupil.
explanation: Adam's actions all show him helping another pupil. The main idea is about his helpful behaviour, not the lunch box itself.

subject: English
question_text: Puan Salmah's class read about sea turtles. Then they watched a short video and made posters about protecting beaches. What is the main idea?
option_a: The class learned about protecting sea turtles.
option_b: The class planned a beach holiday.
option_d: Sea turtles live in school ponds.
explanation: Reading, watching a video, and making posters all focus on sea turtles and beach protection. Together they support the main idea that the class learned how to protect sea turtles.

subject: English
question_text: Kumar woke up late, missed the first bus, and had to ask his father for a ride to school. Which detail best supports the main idea that Kumar had a difficult morning?
option_a: He woke up late.
explanation: Waking up late directly caused the problems that followed. The other choices do not show why his morning was difficult.

subject: English
question_text: At a community event, children painted signs, adults swept the walkways, and volunteers collected rubbish. What is the main idea?
option_a: Everyone worked together to clean the area.
option_b: People came only to paint signs.
option_c: The event was a sports competition.
option_d: The rubbish was left on the ground.
explanation: Different groups did different cleaning jobs. These details show everyone working together to improve the area.

subject: English
question_text: Mira borrowed a mystery book from the library. She read three chapters that evening and continued reading before school the next day. Which detail best supports the idea that Mira enjoyed the book?
option_a: She kept reading whenever she had time.
option_b: The book was from the library.
option_d: She went to school the next day.
explanation: Continuing to read at different times shows strong interest. That detail best supports the idea that Mira enjoyed the book.

subject: English
question_text: The school held a 'No Plastic Day'. Pupils brought reusable bottles and lunch boxes, and the canteen did not give out plastic straws. What is the main idea?
option_a: The school tried to reduce plastic waste.
option_d: The canteen closed for the day.
explanation: Reusable containers and no plastic straws both reduce plastic waste. These details support the main idea.

subject: English
question_text: A storm caused several branches to fall in the neighbourhood. The next morning, residents moved the branches and checked on older neighbours. What is the main idea?
option_a: The residents helped after the storm.
option_c: The storm lasted for a week.
explanation: Moving branches and checking on neighbours are actions people took after the storm. The main idea is that residents helped one another.

subject: English
question_text: Jia Hui wanted to improve her spelling. She wrote difficult words in a notebook, practised them daily, and asked her sister to test her. What is the main idea?
option_a: Jia Hui used several ways to improve spelling.
explanation: The passage gives several study methods Jia Hui used. Together they show that she worked actively to improve her spelling.

subject: English
question_text: The school garden has herbs, vegetables, and flowering plants. Science classes sometimes visit it to observe insects and plant growth. What is the main idea?
option_a: The school garden is used for learning and growing plants.
option_c: Students are not allowed in the garden.
option_d: The garden is used only for sports.
explanation: The garden contains many plants and is also used by science classes. These details support the main idea that it is both a growing and learning space.

subject: English
question_text: Before a class trip, Mr. Lee reminded pupils to bring water, wear comfortable shoes, and stay with their groups. What is the main idea?
option_a: Mr. Lee gave safety and preparation advice for the trip.
option_b: Mr. Lee cancelled the class trip.
option_c: Pupils had to wear uniforms only.
option_d: The trip was to a shoe shop.
explanation: The reminders help pupils prepare and stay safe during the trip. They all support the same main idea.

subject: English
question_text: Nadia sold handmade bookmarks at the school fair for RM3 each. She used the money to buy food for an animal shelter. What is the main idea?
option_a: Nadia raised money to help an animal shelter.
explanation: Selling bookmarks was the method Nadia used to collect money. The purpose was to help the animal shelter.

subject: English
question_text: The football team lost its first two matches. After extra practice, the players communicated better and won the next game. What is the main idea?
option_a: Practice helped the team improve.
explanation: The passage shows a change from losing to winning after extra practice. This supports the main idea that practice helped the team improve.

subject: English
question_text: Read the paragraph: 'For weeks, the Year 5 pupils collected old newspapers. They sorted them carefully and sold them to a recycling centre. The class used the money to buy new plants for the school garden.' Which title best matches the main idea?
option_a: Recycling to Improve the School Garden
explanation: The paragraph connects recycling newspapers with raising money for the school garden. The best title includes both the action and its purpose.

subject: English
question_text: A notice says: 'Bring your own cup on Friday. The canteen will give a 50 sen discount on drinks served in reusable cups.' What is the main purpose of the notice?
option_a: To encourage pupils to use reusable cups
option_b: To make pupils buy more plastic cups
option_d: To advertise a new school uniform
explanation: The discount rewards pupils who bring reusable cups. This shows the notice is meant to encourage reuse and reduce waste.

subject: English
question_text: Read: 'Zarul checked the weather forecast before football practice. Dark clouds were expected, so he packed a small towel and an extra shirt.' Which detail is most important to the main idea?
option_a: He prepared for possible rain.
explanation: The important idea is that Zarul used the forecast to prepare for bad weather. The other details are less central.

subject: English
question_text: A paragraph describes how a family compares prices, makes a shopping list, and uses discount vouchers before buying groceries. What is the best main idea?
option_a: The family plans carefully to save money.
option_b: The family buys everything they see.
option_c: Discount vouchers are hard to find.
explanation: Comparing prices, making a list, and using vouchers are all money-saving strategies. Together they show careful planning.

subject: English
question_text: Read: 'The playground was muddy after heavy rain, so the teacher moved PE class into the hall. Pupils played simple team games indoors instead.' What main idea connects all the details?
option_a: The PE lesson was changed because of wet weather.
explanation: The rain made the playground unsuitable, so the lesson moved indoors. The key idea is the change caused by the weather.

subject: English
question_text: A school article explains that pupils should sleep early, eat breakfast, and prepare their bags the night before exams. What is the main idea?
option_a: Good preparation can help pupils on exam days.
option_c: Breakfast is the only important habit.
explanation: The article gives several preparation habits that can help pupils feel ready for exams. No single habit is the whole main idea.

subject: English
question_text: Read: 'At the charity run, some pupils ran, some handed out water, and others recorded finishing times. Everyone had a job.' Which statement best summarises the passage?
option_a: Different pupils contributed in different ways.
option_b: Only runners helped at the event.
explanation: The details show that people had different roles but all helped the event. That is the best summary of the passage.

subject: English
question_text: A passage explains that mangrove roots reduce wave impact, provide shelter for young fish, and help prevent soil erosion. What is the main idea?
option_a: Mangroves are important to coastal environments.
explanation: The listed details show several ways mangroves protect and support coastal areas. Therefore, their importance is the main idea.

subject: English
question_text: Read: 'Liyana planned to spend RM20 at the book fair. She bought one book for RM12 and a bookmark for RM3, then saved the remaining money.' Which statement best captures the main idea?
option_a: Liyana managed her book fair money carefully.
option_d: The bookmark cost more than the book.
explanation: Liyana stayed within her RM20 budget and even saved some money. This shows careful money management.

subject: English
question_text: A short article gives these details: 'Turn off lights when leaving a room. Unplug chargers when not in use. Use natural light during the day.' What is the article mainly about?
option_a: Ways to save electricity
explanation: Every detail describes an action that reduces electricity use. So the main idea is about saving electricity.

subject: English
question_text: Read: 'The class pet fish stopped eating. The pupils noticed the water looked cloudy, so they told their teacher and cleaned the tank carefully.' Which detail best explains the main idea that the pupils acted responsibly?
option_a: They noticed a problem and took action.
option_b: The fish lived in a tank.
option_c: The tank was made of glass.
explanation: Responsible behaviour means noticing a problem and doing something appropriate about it. That detail directly supports the main idea.

subject: English
question_text: A paragraph says that after moving to a new school, Daniel joined a chess club, introduced himself to classmates, and asked a teacher for help when he felt unsure. What is the best main idea?
option_a: Daniel took steps to adjust to his new school.
option_d: Teachers did all his work for him.
explanation: Joining a club, meeting classmates, and asking for help are all ways Daniel adapted. Together they show his effort to adjust to a new school.

subject: English
question_text: The soup was very hot, so Iman waited for it to cool. What does 'cool' mean here?
option_a: Become less hot
explanation: In this sentence, 'cool' describes the soup becoming less hot. The meaning is shown by the words 'very hot' and 'waited'.

subject: English
question_text: Suresh carried a light bag to school. What does 'light' mean here?
option_a: Not heavy
explanation: Because 'light' describes the bag, it means the bag is not heavy. The other meanings do not fit the sentence.

subject: English
question_text: The children were cheerful after winning the quiz. What does 'cheerful' mean?
option_a: Happy
explanation: Winning the quiz would likely make the children happy. 'Cheerful' means happy and positive.

subject: English
question_text: Nabila whispered because the baby was sleeping. What does 'whispered' mean?
option_a: Spoke very softly
explanation: A sleeping baby should not be disturbed by loud sounds. 'Whispered' means spoke very softly.

subject: English
question_text: The road was narrow, so only one car could pass at a time. What does 'narrow' mean?
option_a: Not wide
explanation: The clue is that only one car could pass at a time. This shows the road was not wide.

subject: English
question_text: Azlan was exhausted after running five kilometres. What does 'exhausted' mean?
option_a: Very tired
explanation: Running a long distance can make someone very tired. 'Exhausted' means extremely tired.

subject: English
question_text: The glass slipped from Mei's hand and shattered on the floor. What does 'shattered' mean?
option_a: Broke into many pieces
explanation: Glass that falls can break into many small pieces. 'Shattered' means broke badly into pieces.

subject: English
question_text: The kitten hid beneath the chair. What does 'beneath' mean?
option_a: Under
explanation: 'Beneath' means under something. The kitten was under the chair.

subject: English
question_text: The teacher praised Amir for his neat handwriting. What does 'praised' mean?
option_a: Said something good about
explanation: The teacher was pleased with Amir's neat work. 'Praised' means spoke positively about it.

subject: English
question_text: The mango was ripe and ready to eat. What does 'ripe' mean?
option_a: Fully grown and ready to eat
explanation: The phrase 'ready to eat' gives the clue. 'Ripe' means the fruit has developed enough to be eaten.

subject: English
question_text: The hall was silent during the speech. What does 'silent' mean?
option_a: Quiet
explanation: During a speech, 'silent' means there was little or no sound. So 'quiet' is the best meaning.

subject: English
question_text: Aqilah glanced at the clock before leaving. What does 'glanced' mean?
option_a: Looked quickly
explanation: 'Glanced' means looked at something briefly or quickly. The clock was checked for a short moment.

subject: English
question_text: The hikers were relieved when they finally saw the rest hut after a long walk. What does 'relieved' most likely mean?
option_a: Feeling less worried or tired because help is near
explanation: Seeing the rest hut after a long walk would remove some worry and tiredness. 'Relieved' means feeling better after stress or difficulty.

subject: English
question_text: The shop was crowded, so Hana had to squeeze between people. What does 'squeeze' mean here?
option_a: Move through a tight space
explanation: The clue is that the shop was crowded. 'Squeeze' means to move through a small or tight space.

subject: English
question_text: Encik Rahman gave a brief talk before the match began. What does 'brief' mean?
option_a: Short
explanation: A 'brief talk' is one that does not take much time. Here, 'brief' means short.

subject: English
question_text: The old wooden bridge looked fragile, so the children crossed it carefully. What does 'fragile' mean?
option_a: Easily broken or damaged
explanation: The children were careful because the bridge could be damaged easily. 'Fragile' means easily broken.

subject: English
question_text: Farah was eager to open the parcel that had arrived from her cousin. What does 'eager' mean?
option_a: Very excited and wanting to do something
explanation: Wanting to open the parcel right away shows strong excitement. 'Eager' means very keen or excited to do something.

subject: English
question_text: The coach asked the players to maintain their focus until the final whistle. What does 'maintain' mean here?
option_a: Keep
explanation: The players need to continue focusing until the end. 'Maintain' means keep something at the same level or state.

subject: English
question_text: The river became shallow near the bank, so the water reached only Amir's ankles. What does 'shallow' mean?
option_a: Not deep
explanation: Water that reaches only the ankles is not deep. That clue shows 'shallow' means not deep.

subject: English
question_text: The principal requested that pupils assemble in the hall at 8:00 a.m. What does 'assemble' mean?
option_a: Gather together
explanation: Pupils going to the hall at the same time are gathering in one place. 'Assemble' means gather together.

subject: English
question_text: The thunder was so sudden that it startled the baby. What does 'startled' mean?
option_a: Surprised or frightened suddenly
explanation: A sudden loud sound can surprise or frighten someone. 'Startled' means suddenly shocked or frightened.

subject: English
question_text: The librarian asked us to handle the old book with care because it was rare. What does 'rare' mean here?
option_a: Uncommon
explanation: An old book that needs special care may be uncommon and difficult to replace. 'Rare' means not commonly found.

subject: English
question_text: Aisyah's answer was accurate, so she received full marks. What does 'accurate' mean?
option_a: Correct and exact
explanation: Receiving full marks shows the answer was correct. 'Accurate' means correct and exact.

subject: English
question_text: The puppy was reluctant to enter the vet's room and kept pulling back. What does 'reluctant' mean?
option_a: Unwilling or hesitant
explanation: Pulling back shows the puppy did not want to enter. 'Reluctant' means unwilling or hesitant.

subject: English
question_text: Read: 'Although the market was usually noisy, it was unusually subdued that morning, with only a few soft voices.' What does 'subdued' most likely mean?
option_a: Quiet and less lively
explanation: The clue 'only a few soft voices' shows the market was quieter than usual. 'Subdued' means calm, quiet, or less lively.

subject: English
question_text: Read: 'The new student hesitated at the classroom door, then slowly stepped inside.' What does 'hesitated' suggest?
option_a: Paused because of uncertainty
explanation: The phrase 'then slowly stepped inside' suggests the student paused before entering. 'Hesitated' means stopped briefly because of uncertainty.

subject: English
question_text: Read: 'After fixing the loose wheel, the mechanic tested the bicycle to ensure it was stable.' What does 'stable' mean here?
option_a: Firm and unlikely to wobble
explanation: A repaired wheel should not wobble. In this context, 'stable' means firm and steady.

subject: English
question_text: Read: 'The teacher's instructions were precise: underline the title, circle three keywords, and write one sentence.' What does 'precise' mean?
option_a: Clear and exact
explanation: The instructions give exact actions to follow. 'Precise' means clear, specific, and exact.

subject: English
question_text: Read: 'The path was slippery after the rain, so the hikers moved cautiously.' What does 'cautiously' mean?
option_a: Carefully to avoid danger
explanation: A slippery path can cause people to fall, so they must move carefully. 'Cautiously' means in a careful way to avoid danger.

subject: English
question_text: Read: 'The teacher noticed a significant improvement in Jia Wei's reading; he could now understand longer passages.' What does 'significant' mean?
option_a: Important or noticeable
explanation: Being able to understand longer passages shows a clear improvement. 'Significant' means important or noticeable.

subject: English
question_text: Read: 'The crowd gradually became smaller as the night market prepared to close.' What does 'gradually' mean?
option_a: Little by little
explanation: The crowd did not disappear immediately. 'Gradually' means something happens slowly, little by little.

subject: English
question_text: Read: 'Sofia gave a convincing explanation, so the group agreed to try her idea.' What does 'convincing' mean?
option_a: Able to make others believe or agree
explanation: The group agreed after hearing Sofia's explanation. This shows it was believable and persuasive.

subject: English
question_text: Read: 'The farmer inspected the leaves closely for signs of damage.' What does 'inspected' mean?
option_a: Examined carefully
explanation: Looking closely for damage means checking something carefully. 'Inspected' means examined in detail.

subject: English
question_text: Read: 'The school launched a campaign to conserve water by fixing leaks and using less water for cleaning.' What does 'conserve' mean?
option_a: Save and use carefully
explanation: Fixing leaks and using less water are ways of saving water. 'Conserve' means protect or use carefully to avoid waste.

subject: English
question_text: Read: 'The kitten was timid at first, hiding whenever someone entered the room.' What does 'timid' mean?
option_a: Shy and easily frightened
explanation: Hiding when people enter suggests the kitten is shy or afraid. 'Timid' means shy and easily frightened.

subject: English
question_text: Read: 'The instructions seemed complicated, but after the teacher demonstrated each step, they became manageable.' What does 'manageable' mean?
option_a: Possible to do without too much difficulty
explanation: After seeing each step, the task became easier to handle. 'Manageable' means possible to do without too much difficulty.

subject: English
question_text: Aiman put on his raincoat and picked up an umbrella before leaving the house. What can you infer?
option_a: It is raining or may rain.
option_b: It is very hot and sunny.
explanation: A raincoat and umbrella are used in wet weather. These clues suggest that it is raining or may rain soon.

subject: English
question_text: Lina yawned several times and rubbed her eyes. What can you infer?
option_a: She is tired.
explanation: Yawning and rubbing the eyes are common signs of tiredness. These clues help us infer that Lina is sleepy or tired.

subject: English
question_text: The classroom lights were off, and all the chairs were empty. What can you infer?
option_a: No class is happening there now.
option_b: The room is full of pupils.
option_d: The teacher is giving a lesson.
explanation: An empty room with the lights off suggests nobody is using it. So it is reasonable to infer that no class is happening there.

subject: English
question_text: Ravi's shoes were muddy after he came home. What can you infer?
option_a: He probably walked somewhere wet or muddy.
explanation: Mud on his shoes is a clue that he walked on wet or muddy ground. The passage does not say this directly, but the evidence supports it.

subject: English
question_text: Nora smelled smoke and heard the fire alarm. What should she most likely do next?
option_a: Leave the building safely.
explanation: Smoke and a fire alarm signal possible danger. The safest prediction is that she should leave the building safely.

subject: English
question_text: The puppy sat beside its empty food bowl and looked at its owner. What can you infer?
option_a: The puppy is probably hungry.
option_c: The puppy is afraid of water.
explanation: An empty food bowl and the puppy's behaviour suggest it wants food. So we can infer that it is hungry.

subject: English
question_text: Hafiz checked his watch and started walking faster toward the bus stop. What can you infer?
option_a: He may be late for the bus.
option_c: He forgot where the bus stop is.
explanation: Checking the time and speeding up are clues that Hafiz may be in a hurry. He likely does not want to miss the bus.

subject: English
question_text: The sky became dark, and strong winds began to blow. What will most likely happen next?
option_a: It may rain soon.
explanation: Dark skies and strong winds often come before rain. These weather clues make rain the most likely prediction.

subject: English
question_text: Sara studied her spelling words every night before the test. What is most likely to happen?
option_a: She may do well on the test.
explanation: Regular practice usually helps a person remember better. So it is reasonable to predict that Sara may perform well.

subject: English
question_text: The ice cream was left on the table in a warm room. What will most likely happen?
option_a: It will melt.
explanation: Ice cream melts when it becomes warm. Since the room is warm, melting is the most likely result.

subject: English
question_text: Firdaus heard thunder and saw lightning outside. What can he infer about the weather?
option_a: A storm is nearby.
option_d: There is no wind or rain anywhere.
explanation: Thunder and lightning are strong clues of a storm. Therefore, Firdaus can infer that stormy weather is nearby.

subject: English
question_text: Mia's lunch box was empty after recess, and she smiled. What can you infer?
option_a: She probably ate her lunch.
option_c: She is still very hungry for the same lunch.
option_d: The lunch box is brand new.
explanation: An empty lunch box after recess suggests the food was eaten. Her smile also supports the idea that she was satisfied.

subject: English
question_text: Arjun saw a long queue at the canteen and only five minutes of recess left. What is he most likely to do?
option_a: Choose a shorter queue or a quick snack.
option_b: Join the longest queue and move slowly.
explanation: With little time left, Arjun will likely choose a faster option. The clues are the long queue and short remaining recess.

subject: English
question_text: Nadia found that the library book's cover was torn when she took it from her bag. She remembered her water bottle had leaked. What can she infer?
option_a: The water probably damaged the book.
option_c: The book was damaged by sunlight.
explanation: A leaking water bottle could wet and weaken the book. This clue makes water damage the most reasonable inference.

subject: English
question_text: Aisyah's team has practised its presentation several times and corrected all unclear parts. What is most likely to happen during the presentation?
option_a: They will present more confidently.
option_b: They will forget the whole topic immediately.
option_d: They will have no idea what to say.
explanation: Practice and corrections usually improve confidence and readiness. Therefore, a more confident presentation is the best prediction.

subject: English
question_text: The playground is wet, and the PE teacher is carrying cones into the school hall. What can pupils infer?
option_a: PE may be held indoors.
option_b: PE has been cancelled for the year.
explanation: The wet playground and cones being moved indoors suggest a change of location. It is reasonable to infer that PE may be held in the hall.

subject: English
question_text: Danish put RM5 into his savings box every week for a month. What can you predict?
option_a: He will have more money saved than before.
option_b: He will have less money than he started with.
option_c: His savings box will be empty.
option_d: He will owe the box money.
explanation: Adding money each week increases the total savings. So he will have more money saved after a month.

subject: English
question_text: The teacher wrote 'Bring coloured paper and glue tomorrow' on the board. What can pupils predict?
option_a: They may do an art or craft activity.
option_b: They will have a swimming lesson.
option_c: They will cook in the canteen.
option_d: They will take a maths test only.
explanation: Coloured paper and glue are common materials for craft work. These clues suggest an art or craft activity.

subject: English
question_text: A cat keeps scratching at the door and looking outside. What can you infer?
option_a: It probably wants to go out.
option_b: It wants to read a book.
option_c: It is asking for a pencil.
explanation: Scratching at the door and looking outside are clues that the cat wants the door opened. It most likely wants to go out.

subject: English
question_text: The bus driver announces that the road ahead is flooded and the bus will take another route. What is most likely to happen?
option_a: The journey may take longer.
option_b: The bus will fly over the flood.
option_c: Everyone will arrive earlier for sure.
option_d: The bus will turn into a boat.
explanation: Taking another route often adds extra distance or time. Therefore, the journey may take longer.

subject: English
question_text: Farah notices that her plant is leaning toward the window. What can she infer?
option_a: The plant is growing toward the light.
option_c: The window is pulling the plant.
option_d: The plant is trying to leave the pot.
explanation: Plants often grow toward a light source. Since the plant leans toward the window, light is the most reasonable explanation.

subject: English
question_text: Hakim forgot to charge his tablet, and the battery shows 2% before class. What is likely to happen?
option_a: The tablet may switch off soon.
option_b: The battery will instantly become full.
explanation: A 2% battery level is very low. Without charging, the tablet is likely to switch off soon.

subject: English
question_text: The school bell rings, and pupils start packing their books into bags. What can you infer?
option_a: The lesson is ending or has ended.
option_d: The school is closed for a month.
explanation: Packing books after the bell is a common sign that class is finishing. These clues support that inference.

subject: English
question_text: Kavitha brought a reusable bag and a shopping list to the supermarket. What can you infer?
option_a: She plans to shop in an organised way.
option_d: She wants to buy a school desk.
explanation: A shopping list helps organise purchases, and a reusable bag is meant for carrying them. Together they suggest planned shopping.

subject: English
question_text: Read: 'The school field was covered with puddles after overnight rain. At 7:30 a.m., the sports teacher sent a message asking pupils to report to the hall.' What is the best inference?
option_a: The sports activity will probably be moved indoors.
option_b: The school field is ready for use.
option_d: Pupils will be sent home for a week.
explanation: The wet field is unsuitable for outdoor sports, and pupils are told to go to the hall. These clues strongly suggest an indoor activity instead.

subject: English
question_text: Read: 'Nurul had RM15. She chose a book costing RM12, then noticed a bookmark priced at RM5. She put the bookmark back.' Why did she most likely do this?
option_a: She did not have enough money for both items.
option_d: She had RM50 more in her bag.
explanation: The book and bookmark together would cost RM17, which is more than RM15. So the best inference is that she could not afford both.

subject: English
question_text: Read: 'During group work, Ethan kept looking at the clock. When the teacher said, “Five minutes left,” he quickly divided the remaining tasks among his friends.' What can you infer about Ethan?
option_a: He is aware of the time and wants the group to finish.
option_b: He wants the group to stop working.
explanation: Looking at the clock and quickly organising tasks show that Ethan is managing time. He wants the group to complete the work before time runs out.

subject: English
question_text: Read: 'The café usually has many customers at lunchtime. Today, several tables are empty, and a sign outside says “Heavy rain warning”.' What is the best inference?
option_a: The weather may have reduced the number of customers.
option_b: The café has run out of tables.
option_c: The café is more crowded than usual.
option_d: The sign is advertising sunny weather.
explanation: Heavy rain can make people less likely to go out. The empty tables support the inference that the weather reduced customer numbers.

subject: English
question_text: Read: 'Mei Ling's plant had yellow leaves. She moved it away from the dark corner and placed it near a bright window.' What does she probably believe?
option_a: The plant needs more light.
option_c: The plant needs to be hidden.
option_d: The yellow leaves are caused by books.
explanation: Moving the plant toward a bright window shows Mei Ling thinks light may help it. Her action reveals what she believes.

subject: English
question_text: Read: 'The class had planned an outdoor picnic. By noon, thunder could be heard and the teacher began moving food boxes into the canteen.' What will most likely happen next?
option_a: The picnic will be moved indoors.
option_b: The class will sit outside in the storm.
option_c: The food will be thrown away.
explanation: Thunder suggests bad weather, and the teacher is already moving food inside. The most likely next event is an indoor picnic.

subject: English
question_text: Read: 'Aiman's bicycle chain kept slipping. He stopped riding, checked the chain, and walked the bicycle home.' What can you infer about Aiman's decision?
option_a: He chose safety instead of continuing to ride.
option_b: He wanted to make the chain worse.
option_c: He was late for a race and sped up.
option_d: He did not notice any problem.
explanation: A slipping chain can make cycling unsafe. By walking the bicycle home, Aiman showed that safety was more important than continuing to ride.

subject: English
question_text: Read: 'The librarian placed a sign saying “New books this week” near a shelf. Several pupils gathered there during recess.' What is the most likely reason?
option_a: The pupils are interested in the new books.
option_c: The pupils are waiting for a bus.
explanation: The sign announces new books, and pupils gather near that shelf. The strongest inference is that they are interested in seeing the new books.

subject: English
question_text: Read: 'Sofia practised a difficult piano piece every evening. At first she stopped often, but after two weeks she could play it without pausing.' What can you infer?
option_a: Regular practice helped her improve.
option_b: The piano became easier by itself.
option_c: She stopped practising after one day.
explanation: Her performance improved over the same period that she practised regularly. This supports the inference that practice helped her improve.

subject: English
question_text: Read: 'A family planned to visit the beach, but the weather app showed thunderstorms all afternoon. They packed board games instead.' What are they most likely planning?
option_a: To stay indoors and play games.
option_c: To cancel all family activities forever.
option_d: To play board games in the sea.
explanation: Thunderstorms make outdoor beach activities unsafe or unpleasant. Packing board games suggests they are preparing for indoor time.

subject: English
question_text: Read: 'The canteen introduced a fruit cup for RM2.50. By the end of the week, the fruit cups often sold out before recess ended.' What can you infer?
option_a: The fruit cups are popular with pupils.
option_c: The fruit cups are too expensive for everyone.
explanation: Selling out early usually means many people are buying the item. So the fruit cups are likely popular.

subject: English
question_text: Read: 'Before the science quiz, Harith reviewed his notes, asked questions about topics he did not understand, and slept early. What is the best prediction?
option_a: He is likely to feel better prepared for the quiz.
option_b: He will definitely get every answer wrong.
option_c: He will forget he has a quiz.
option_d: He will arrive without knowing the subject.
explanation: Reviewing notes, asking questions, and getting enough rest are useful preparation steps. These actions make it likely that Harith will feel more prepared.
